data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word ‘Amrut’ meaning ‘Immortal’ or ‘Nectar of Life’. In Hindu mythology, ‘Amrut’ is the divine nectar that grants immortality. The name Amish carries the meaning “Immortal” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Amish usually hope their child will grow to embody immortal and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Embrace the divine nectar of life.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Amish total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.
